answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: every agent must lock a non-trivial stake before it can act, so spinning up a swarm of fake clones stops being cheap. A sybil attacker reaching for the zenith of influence would have to post capital per identity, and provable misbehavior burns that bond. Honest agents accrue reputation like slowly polished jade, while a brand-new identity carries only a whisper of voting weight until it has earned trust through costly, verifiable work.
